title: Scenic design is really going above and beyond this season #thecottag...
transcript: I finally went to go see the cottage, which is a new comedy playing on Broadway. It closes October 29th, so it is a limited run. And this is a hilarious comedy about a cottage that is used primarily for sexual escapades. Let's say there has been some debate over whether this play is a farce or not. And I think that when this play is at its. As it is very farcical, the comedy is very absurd. These situations are completely improbable. And when this is over the top, it is at its best. In fact, if I had any criticism about this show, it would be that it isn't consistently as over the top as I would have wanted it to be. One of my favorite things about comedies is when they really build up to this really grand and absurd ending. And this, for me, was kind of missing that. But it. When it's good, it's really, really good and really, really funny. The performances in this are hilarious. Especially Dan Steingold and Alex Moffat are both just tremendously funny. I also really loved Eric Mccormick in this, but I feel like he was almost underused. And there are some really good gags in this play. I just almost wish that they were spread out a little more throughout the show. There's an ongoing gag in one that is used a lot and then just kind of goes away. And ultimately, the end, for me just didn't pack The punch that I wanted it to considering how funny the first act is. Overall, I'm really glad I saw this. And if you're a fan of really over the top comedy, I would recommend seeing this. Especially the cast and the set are worth trying to get into this theater before it closes October 29th.
